sections.heading: What kukuri is
paragraphs: kukuri is a decentralized application built on a P2P foundation. The operator is {{controllerName}} and the contact address is {{contact}}. The operator's legal name and address will be provided without delay on request to that address.
The operator controls only the distribution, updates, information, and Community Node capabilities it provides. A central authority that governs the entire network does not structurally exist.

After consent, the app may contact the destination and an image host specified by that page to preview the first external URL in a public post. URLs in private channels and DMs are not fetched automatically.

sections.heading: Definitions and responsibility boundaries
paragraphs: A user is a person who accepts these terms; a person who posts is a user who shares content; and a receiving user is a person who receives it within the selected audience. A Community Node is an optional support service and may be operated by a third party independent of the operator.

Third parties on P2P include receiving users, peers, third-party Nodes, relays, the DHT, and network providers. The operator and each Node operator control only services they provide and content or traffic in which they actually participate.

sections.heading: Eligibility and adult material
paragraphs: kukuri may only be used by people who are 18 years of age or older. By starting to use kukuri, you represent that you are 18 or older.

Display of adult material is disabled by default. To display it, you must explicitly enable it yourself in the settings screen. Adult material is identified by labels self-declared by the person who posted it and may also be informed by labels estimated by Community Nodes you configured. Such an estimate is that node's judgment, not a decision by the operator or by kukuri as a whole, and you can choose in the settings which nodes' estimates to use. The absence of a label does not guarantee that a post is free of adult material.

If you place a Community Node in your adoption order in the settings screen, posts from people that node rates low may be collapsed. Such a rating is that node's judgment, not a decision by the operator or by kukuri as a whole. Collapsing affects display only: it does not change how posts are fetched or stored, nor your notifications, blocks, or mutes. You can undo it for a single post or for a single person.

You can share your own blocks and mutes with a Community Node only if you accept the optional consent document that node publishes. Sharing is off by default and you can revoke it at any time, which requests deletion of the records stored on that node.

sections.heading: Prohibited uses
paragraphs: Using kukuri for unlawful purposes, or creating, sharing, or distributing child sexual abuse / exploitation (CSAM / CSE) or other critical rights-violating content, is prohibited.

Infringing the rights of others (intellectual property, privacy, reputation, etc.), disrupting the network, community nodes, or relays, and using kukuri for malware, phishing, or other malicious purposes are prohibited.

sections.heading: Ownership of your content
paragraphs: Copyright and other rights in text, images, audio, video, models, attachments, and other content you post or share remain, as a rule, with you or the lawful rightsholder.
Sharing content through kukuri does not by itself transfer those rights to the developers, the default community node, or any other Community Node.

sections.heading: Your rights and permissions
paragraphs: You represent that you own the necessary rights in any work, likeness, name, audio, video, 3D model, attachment, or other content you post or share, or have permission from the lawful rightsholder for the sharing and technical processing described here.
When quoting, reposting, editing, or combining third-party content, you are responsible for complying with applicable law and license terms.

sections.heading: Your responsibilities
paragraphs: You are responsible for content you create or share and for selecting its audience. Public posts may be copied to unrestricted receiving users and participating Nodes; even in a private channel or DM, designated recipients may retain a copy after receiving it.
Providing the app does not mean that posts are pre-screened, that their legality, accuracy, or safety is guaranteed, or that all P2P traffic is monitored.

sections.heading: Limited technical license
paragraphs: To make communication, display, and synchronization work within the audience you select, you grant receiving users in that audience a non-exclusive, royalty-free license only to receive, copy, store locally, display, and synchronize the content. This is not a transfer of ownership.

A public-topic post is shared with receiving users that obtain that topic. Private channels and DMs are limited to their designated receiving users and may not be repurposed for a public topic or an unrestricted audience.

Docs handle text and metadata, and blobs handle attachments, within the selected audience. Hints only announce updates and do not expand the audience or license. Connectivity features only assist connections and do not grant rights to use content for another purpose.
Any license to a Community Node is limited by that node's per-node terms, capabilities that are actually enabled, authority scope, and content in which that node is involved.
No lasting or comprehensive network-wide rights are granted to disabled capabilities, uninvolved nodes, other nodes, the default node, or the kukuri project.

sections.heading: After withdrawal
paragraphs: A compatible client or node that recognizes a valid withdrawal by the user who posted it, or a node-local transmission block, stops future display, indexing, search, discovery, recommendation, synchronization, retrieval, caching, or delivery within its applicable scope. Records may be retained only where required by law and with their subject, purpose, and duration limited.

Copies already obtained by receiving peers or third-party nodes before withdrawal cannot be guaranteed to be remotely recovered or erased. Withdrawal does not mean immediate, complete deletion from the entire network.

sections.heading: Uses not licensed
paragraphs: The limited license does not include the right to use content for advertising, promotion, generative-AI training, machine-learning model training, or another independent secondary purpose.
It does not permit bypassing private-channel or DM access controls, expanding the selected audience, or repurposing content for a different public use.

sections.heading: Reports and restrictions
paragraphs: You may report content to a Community Node that actually participated in its delivery, indexing, moderation, or caching. If no participating service can be identified, neither the operator nor the default Node is guaranteed to act as a central reporting desk for the entire network.

The operator and each Node operator may apply implemented restrictions within distribution, updates, or Node capabilities they control in response to prohibited conduct, security risks, or legal requirements. They cannot collectively disable third-party Nodes, receiving devices, or Direct P2P.

sections.heading: Account-identifying key
paragraphs: You are responsible for your account-identifying key and backup passphrase. The operator does not normally obtain your secret key and cannot centrally reissue, reset, or recover a lost key.
kukuri provides key export/import and encrypted device backup/restore, but these do not erase third-party copies, remotely disable an existing device, or automatically synchronize all devices.

sections.heading: Community Nodes
paragraphs: A Community Node is an optional support service. For each Node, review its operator, capabilities, responsibility scope, terms, privacy policy, external transmissions, and retention policy and accept them separately from the app-level documents.

A Node's license and responsibility are limited to its per-node terms, capabilities actually enabled, authority scope, and content in which it participates. Declining or losing a Node does not collectively disable local data or Direct P2P that remains technically available.

sections.heading: Changes, interruption, and termination
paragraphs: The operator may change, interrupt, or terminate distribution, updates, information, or Node capabilities it provides for security, maintenance, failures, legal requirements, or another reasonable operational reason. Material planned changes will be announced in advance where reasonably possible.
Ending an operator service or a particular Node does not collectively terminate or erase third-party Nodes, receiving users' copies, local data, or Direct P2P that remains technically available.

sections.heading: Open-source license
paragraphs: kukuri software is governed by the repository's MIT License and the licenses of third-party components. These terms govern services and posted content; where they conflict over software use, the applicable open-source license controls.
Content you post does not become subject to the MIT License or another open-source license merely because it is shared through kukuri.

sections.heading: Limitation of liability
paragraphs: kukuri is provided as-is. The operator does not warrant continuous reachability, completeness, security, or freedom from data loss for peers, third-party Nodes, relays, the DHT, network paths, or other environments outside its control.

Except for intentional misconduct or gross negligence, liability is limited to ordinary and direct loss arising from services the operator itself provides. No exclusion or limitation applies where it is invalid under the Consumer Contract Act or another mandatory law.
Each Community Node operator's liability is governed by that Node's terms and applicable law.

sections.heading: Governing law and agreed jurisdiction
paragraphs: These terms and the relationship between you and the operator are governed by Japanese law. Unless mandatory law provides otherwise, the Tokyo District Court or Tokyo Summary Court has exclusive agreed jurisdiction as the court of first instance.

sections.heading: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: The operator may change these terms when the change benefits users generally or is reasonable in light of its necessity, appropriateness, and related circumstances. The change, updated terms, and effective date will be notified or published by an appropriate method.

For a significant update, the document version is increased and the updated terms are shown for renewed acceptance before network connections resume. Japanese is authoritative and controls over this reference translation if they differ.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.changeSummary: Version 8 adds what may be sent for public-post link previews, what is not sent, and the temporary local retention.

sections.heading: Controller and basic approach
paragraphs: The controller is {{controllerName}} and the contact address is {{contact}}. The operator's name and address will be provided without delay when requested through that address.

Some information, such as your account-identifying secret key, settings, and consent records, remains local. Profiles, public follows, posts, reactions, and attachments are replicated to P2P participants according to the audience you select.

sections.heading: Information shared over P2P
paragraphs: Public profiles, public follows, public posts, replies, reposts, reactions, and attachments are replicated to peers that obtain the relevant user's profile replica or topic.

Private channels are limited to participants holding the capability, and DMs are limited to the designated peer. You cannot completely erase a copy already obtained by another participant from your device alone.

sections.heading: Connectivity and Community Nodes
paragraphs: Public keys, endpoint identifiers, IP addresses, and connection metadata can be observed by the Mainline DHT, peers, configured Community Nodes, iroh relays, and network providers. Routes are selected in the order Direct P2P, Relay Supported P2P, and Relay Fallback.

Depending on the capabilities you accept, a Community Node may receive authentication proofs, endpoint data, topic rendezvous keys, search queries, indexing requests, indexing status checks (the state of your own requests and whether a target is indexed), lookups of adult material estimates (the IDs of posts you view and the identifiers of their attachments, sent only to nodes whose estimates you use; post text, browsing history, and connection data are not sent, and responses are not stored), trust evaluation lookups (the public keys of the people who posted what you view, of the source of a quote or repost, and of the hosts in the live and game lists you view, sent only to nodes you placed in your adoption order; post text, browsing history, and your own block or mute lists are not sent, and responses are used on your device only, then refreshed or discarded once they expire), optional sharing of your blocks and mutes (only if you accept that node's optional consent document: the other party's public key, the kind and state of the action, its time, and your signature; you can revoke at any time, which requests deletion of the stored records), and report or feedback fields. A Node operator is not necessarily the kukuri operator; use the Node manifest to review its retention and external-transmission documents.

sections.heading: Link previews, automatic update checks, and diagnostic reports
paragraphs: After consent, when an eligible settled public post enters the viewport, the app may contact the destination of its first URL and an OGP image host to show a preview. They can observe your IP address, HTTP/TLS request metadata, and the URL path and query. Cookies, authorization, Referer, account/topic/post identifiers, and other post text are not sent. Private channels, DMs, and collapsed content are not fetched automatically, and preview data does not survive an app restart.

After consent, Direct/NSIS and Linux builds check GitHub Releases automatically at startup, every 30 minutes, and when you request a check. GitHub and network providers can observe your IP address and HTTP/TLS request metadata. Microsoft Store builds delegate updates to the Store and Windows and do not send update checks from kukuri to GitHub or a separate Store update API.

A diagnostic report can include app version, platform/user agent, connectivity state, peer and topic counts, and Node URL/session/error information. Copying or exporting does not send it automatically. Secret keys, auth tokens, private capabilities, invitations, DM bodies, and local database paths are excluded by default.

sections.heading: Age attestation, analytics, and deletion limits
paragraphs: Your statement that you are 18 or older is stored locally as a self-attestation. kukuri does not collect your date of birth or official ID and does not perform official age verification. The current app does not enable behavioral analytics, advertising tracking, or automatic crash-report uploads by default.
Local deletion or withdrawal cannot guarantee complete deletion of copies or caches already held by peers or third-party Nodes, or logs held by the DHT, relays, or network providers.

sections.heading: Consent and change history
paragraphs: The app asks you to accept the terms and this policy before starting network connections. A material update increments the document version and requires renewed consent before networking resumes. Version 8 describes what may be sent for public-post link previews.
